zh.title: 單機天花板
zh.question: SQLite WAL 的單機客戶端，什麼信號出現就該拆 Postgres 或佇列？

analyst.reasoning: 信號是寫入者數目、第二台主機、不能丟的工作、以及備份是否在拷貝活的 WAL。不是行數的吉祥數字，也不是「感覺該換企業資料庫了」。先列會改變架構的變量，再談口味。
analyst.answer: 該拆的信號是第二個寫入者，或一份不能丟的工作。不是某一整數的列。
analyst.review: 「別人很晚才拆」是軼事。沒有你的寫入鎖等待，軼事不能當門檻。

researcher.reasoning: 單機聊天應用留在 SQLite 上的時間，通常比文章承認的更長。公開可核對的分界不是百萬列，而是第二個會寫同一檔的程序，或第二台主機。我沒有這座安裝的遙測，就不編一個列數。
researcher.answer: 常見分界是第二個寫入者，不是一個好看的列數。沒有遙測就不要報數。
researcher.review: 你要一個等待毫秒數。沒有這座庫的樣本，那個數是裝飾。先說信號，再等樣本。

engineer.reasoning: WAL 加一個寫入程序，是這個規模的設計。第二個 uvicorn worker 寫同一個檔，是第一個謊。備份若直接拷貝活的 WAL 而不做 checkpoint，是第二個。拆 Postgres 解決不了你還沒有第二台機器這件事。
engineer.answer: 一個寫入者，留在 SQLite WAL。第二個寫入者出現，再拆。不要為了圖上的方框先拆。
engineer.review: 活 WAL 的備份確實是失敗模式。修復是 checkpoint 和一致快照，不是因為害怕就搬去另一個引擎。

critic.reasoning: 失敗模式不是「SQLite 很玩具」。是部署同時拉起兩個寫入者，或備份拷走一個還沒 checkpoint 的 WAL，然後把那個檔叫做備份。換引擎不會讓這兩個操作變正確。
critic.answer: 先禁止第二個寫入者，再談換庫。兩個寫入者打在 Postgres 上，仍然是兩個寫入者。
critic.review: 你把「一個程序」說成永久設計。程序會被複製。若啟動腳本不能保證單一寫入者，設計只存在於README。

strategist.reasoning: 留下，直到你有第二台主機，或一條不能丟的佇列。為了美觀拆開，是把運維面提前買進來。佇列的理由不是「比較專業」，是工作掉了會不會被發現。
strategist.answer: 沒有第二台主機、沒有不能丟的工作，就留在單機 WAL。
strategist.review: 「留到第二個寫入者」要寫進啟動約束，不能只寫進建議。建議不會在凌晨擋住第二個 worker。

writer.reasoning: 這句話會被寫進 README，所以不能比會議更滿。不能寫「SQLite 永遠夠用」。可以寫「這個規模不需要 Postgres」。讀者要知道什麼信號會改這句話。
writer.answer: README 只承諾這個規模。信號出現，句子就作廢。
writer.review: 「留下」若沒有信號，讀起來像口味。把第二個寫入者寫進同一句，句子才是合約。

quant.reasoning: 一個寫入者、fsync、checkpoint。我能量的是形狀，不是這座庫今晚的毫秒。寫入鎖等待若出現在請求路徑上，你已經晚了。若仍然只有一個程序，你還早。沒有樣本，我不報一個假的 P99。
quant.answer: 請求路徑上出現寫入鎖等待，就晚了。只有一個寫入者，就還早。中間沒有魔法列數。
quant.review: 「不能丟的工作」需要一個丟失率，不然每個定時任務都會被說成不能丟。

chair.reasoning: 沒有人用列數當門檻。分歧在於：單一寫入者是設計，還是只是今晚的運氣。紅隊要的是啟動約束，不是另一個引擎。
chair.answer: 留在 SQLite WAL，直到第二個寫入者，或一份不能丟的工作。信號是爭用和第二台主機，不是某一整數的列。換 Postgres 不會把兩個寫入者變成一個。

en.title: Single-node ceiling
en.question: For a single-node client on SQLite WAL, what signal means it is time to split out Postgres or a queue?

analyst.reasoning: The variables that change the architecture are writer count, a second host, a job you cannot lose, and whether backup copies a live WAL. Not an auspicious row count, and not the feeling that it is time for an enterprise database. List the variables before the taste.
analyst.answer: Split on a second writer, or on a job you cannot lose. Not on a round number of rows.
analyst.review: “Others split late” is an anecdote. Without your lock-wait, an anecdote is not a threshold.

researcher.reasoning: Single-node chat apps stay on SQLite longer than essays admit. The checkable split is not a million rows. It is a second process writing the same file, or a second host. This install has no telemetry in the room, so I will not invent a row count.
researcher.answer: The usual split is a second writer, not a photogenic row count. No telemetry, no number.
researcher.review: You want a wait in milliseconds. Without a sample from this database, that number is decoration. Name the signal, then wait for the sample.

engineer.reasoning: WAL plus one writer is the design at this size. A second uvicorn worker on the same file is the first lie. A backup that copies a live WAL without a checkpoint is the second. Postgres does not give you the second machine you do not have.
engineer.answer: One writer: stay on SQLite WAL. When a second writer appears, split. Do not split for a box on a diagram.
engineer.review: A live-WAL backup is a real failure mode. The fix is a checkpoint and a consistent snapshot, not a new engine chosen out of fear.

critic.reasoning: The failure mode is not “SQLite is a toy.” It is a deploy that starts two writers, or a backup that copies a WAL before checkpoint and then calls that file a backup. A new engine does not make either operation correct.
critic.answer: Forbid the second writer before you talk about a new database. Two writers on Postgres are still two writers.
critic.review: You called “one process” a permanent design. Processes get copied. If the start script cannot guarantee a single writer, the design exists only in the README.

strategist.reasoning: Stay until you have a second host, or a queue whose loss would be noticed. Splitting for aesthetics buys the operations surface early. The reason for a queue is not that it looks professional. It is whether a dropped job is visible.
strategist.answer: No second host and no job you cannot lose: stay on one-node WAL.
strategist.review: “Stay until the second writer” has to be a start-up constraint, not advice. Advice will not stop a second worker at 03:00.

writer.reasoning: This sentence will land in a README, so it cannot claim more than the room claimed. Do not write “SQLite is always enough.” You can write “this size does not need Postgres.” The reader has to see which signal retires the sentence.
writer.answer: The README promises this size only. When the signal appears, the sentence expires.
writer.review: “Stay” without a signal reads as taste. Put the second writer in the same sentence and it becomes a contract.

quant.reasoning: One writer, fsync, checkpoint. I can describe the shape. I cannot give tonight’s milliseconds for a database we did not sample. If write-lock wait shows up on the request path, you are late. If there is still one process, you are early. No sample, no fake P99.
quant.answer: Lock wait on the request path means you are late. One writer means you are early. There is no magic row count in between.
quant.review: “A job you cannot lose” needs a loss rate. Otherwise every scheduled task gets called irreplaceable.

chair.reasoning: Nobody used a row count as the threshold. The fight is whether a single writer is a design or tonight’s luck. Red Team wants a start-up constraint, not another engine.
chair.answer: Stay on SQLite WAL until a second writer, or a job you cannot lose. The signal is contention and a second host, not a round number of rows. Postgres will not turn two writers into one.
